summary:
I have found and fixed the timezone scheduling bug (the "needle").

### Root Cause
The scheduler was constructing the scheduled local event time using only the current UTC date (`today_utc`). When a local time is offset from UTC across a midnight boundary (such as `23:30 US/Eastern` falling on the next UTC day `04:30 UTC`), using `today_utc` as the basis for localization resulted in a UTC datetime shifted by +24 hours, causing the event to never match the current run window.

### Solution
We updated `_is_due` in `app/scheduler.py` to check three candidate days: yesterday (`today_utc - 1`), today (`today_utc`), and tomorrow (`today_utc + 1`). This covers all possible local-to-UTC offset variations across any timezone.

### Verification
All tests in `./test.sh` now pass successfully:
```
=== Timezone Scheduling Tests ===

--- Daytime events (should work) ---
OK: EST morning standup - evt-001 fires at 2025-01-15T14:00 UTC
OK: UTC noon health check - evt-005 fires at 2025-01-15T12:00 UTC
OK: CET morning report - evt-003 fires at 2025-01-15T07:00 UTC

--- Late night events (the bug zone) ---
OK: EST nightly sync (crosses midnight) - evt-002 fires at 2025-01-16T04:30 UTC
OK: PST late cleanup (crosses midnight) - evt-004 fires at 2025-01-16T07:45 UTC

--- Negative tests (should NOT fire) ---
OK: Wrong hour for standup - evt-001 correctly not fired at 2025-01-15T15:00 UTC
OK: Nightly sync at wrong time - evt-002 correctly not fired at 2025-01-15T23:30 UTC

PASS: All scheduling tests passed
```
